pr_title: Add beatmap set level pooling to beatmap carousel
pr_comments:
In the above isolated benchmark, performance looks to be slightly improved:

![IMG_0729](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/191335/95883659-2a4f9680-0db6-11eb-9a8e-b94cc7344693.jpeg)

There is some extra overhead attributed to transform trackers, of which a portion is recovered via https://github.com/ppy/osu-framework/pull/3933.

issue_context.title: Panels in beatmap carousel don't pop open correctly after scrolling past the end
issue_context.body:
**Describe the bug:** 
After you scroll past the end of the beatmap carousel, sets directly after sets with many difficulties (like 8+ difficulties it seems) start popping open with incorrect vertical positions for their set panels. 

Expected result: set panel should appear above all its difficulty panels 

Actual result: set panel appears inside or below its difficulty panels

**Screenshots or videos showing encountered issue:** 
https://youtu.be/Cikc8jMDllM

"[Okaerinasai](https://osu.ppy.sh/beatmapsets/395642)" and "[Sore wa Chiisana Hikari no Youna](https://osu.ppy.sh/beatmapsets/430934)" are the beatmaps effected here because "[MIIRO vs. Ai no Scenario](https://osu.ppy.sh/beatmapsets/325158)" and "[Sakebe](https://osu.ppy.sh/beatmapsets/550344)" both have many difficulties.

**osu!lazer version:**
2020.320.1

review_comments: This is also susceptible to asymmetry as far as I can tell, also due to using the top Y coordinate. Either subtracting 1 or using the item's bottom Y position should resolve.

This is resolved in the code just below:

https://github.com/ppy/osu/pull/10494/files/e662dc5342b26ecedd265b55c121a058006e2ad3#diff-0b1dcf0afe266751400b0c7b7256a23274dc0cab9fc8aab278cf2ce804be079cR658-R660

The comment hopefully explains why it needs to be done like this (the set may be visible and have children – offsetting by one means we don't have to account for this on an item level).

Sure, but technically speaking there should be no need to add 1 to the last index if so, because the binary search already guarantees that the set whose index is returned has no overlap with the visible range (its top Y coordinate is either greater than or equal than the upper Y bound).

It's sort of a nitpick though. Shouldn't really ever matter I don't think.
Yeah, probably can remove the +1 on the last index. I just left it there for safety (and as you say, it doesn't really matter as there's no need for 100% accuracy here).

nit: it's test code, but this could be replaced by:

```suggestion
                string version = BeatmapDifficultyManager.GetDifficultyRating(diff).Humanize();
```
I don't think it can, since they don't match. Some of the tests rely on specific strings and would need to be updated, wasn't really wanting to do so.

These DLWs are getting replaced after every `Item` set. I don't think this will necessarily leak memory, but should probably make sure to unsubscribe on the old ones before doing this, for sanity's sake.

I don't think this needs to be done. I consciously made the choice not to unbind because it doesn't need to happen.

It can't possibly leak memory, either.
